summary: Carl Johan Sverdrup Marstrander was a linguist who studied at the University of Oslo (1903–1907) under Sophus Bugge and Alf Torp. He was a professor at the School of Irish Learning (1909–1913) and the University of Oslo (1913–1953).

Carl Maria Franz Lorinser worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Breslau (1839–1841), Sapienza University of Rome (1842–1844), and the University of Munich (~1843–1844), where he earned a Dr. Theol.

Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under mentor John Y. Fenton and held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Humboldt University of Berlin, later serving as Lektor (1847) and professor (1857) at the University of Oslo.
Carl Rabe was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau (~1841–1845), completing his Ph.D. under the supervision of Adolf Friedrich Stenzler.

Carl Salemann was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University (~1867–1875), he held posts there (~1876–1916), served at the Russian Academy of Sciences, and directed the Asiatic Museum from 1890.
Carl Schuster was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Harvard University (~1927–1930) and the University of Vienna (~1932–1934).

Carl Schütz worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1823–1827), under Franz Bopp (~1827–1830), and at the University of Jena (~1830–1831), later teaching modern languages at Ratsgymnasium Bielefeld (1834–1858).

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, as well as teachers Sonam Germano, William A. Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried was a scholar of religion, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Bonn under scholars including Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Trinity College Dublin, several secondary schools, and the University of Jena (1875–1901).
Carl Suneson was an Indologist who studied at Stockholm University (1960–1966) under Siegfried Lienhard and V. Raghavan. In 1966, he became a Docent at Stockholm University.

Carl Theodor Johannsen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Kiel University and the University of Bonn, later teaching at Bonn (1830–1831), Kiel (1831–1833), and the University of Copenhagen as professor of oriental philology and literature (1833).

Carl W. Ernst is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at Stanford (A.B.) and Harvard (Ph.D.). He taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and served as Kenan Distinguished Professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, later holding professorships in Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

Carl William Belser worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Michigan and Leipzig under Friedrich Delitzsch, he taught at Mount Morris, Carthage, the University of Michigan, and served as Latin Department Head at the University of Colorado Boulder (1893).

Carl von Noorden was a historian and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Bonn, Paris, and Berlin under Martin Haug and Leopold von Ranke. He was a professor of history at Greifswald, Marburg, Tübingen, Bonn, and Leipzig (1877).

Carl-Martin Edsman was a religious studies scholar who studied at Uppsala University (~1930–1940), Lund University, and the University of Paris. He held academic posts at Lund University (~1948–1950) and Uppsala University (~1950–1977).

Carlo Bernheimer was a scholar in Indology. He studied at the University of Bologna (~1896–1900) under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè and later served as Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Bologna from 1906 to 1938 and in 1945.
Carlo Della Casa was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Turin (~1945–1949) under Mario Vallauri (~1946–1950) and later held a post at the University of Palermo (~1969–1972).

Carlo Formichi was an Indologist who studied at Naples, Vienna under Georg Bühler, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held teaching posts in Sanskrit at Naples, Pisa, Bologna, and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).
